metadata.description: London after Stamen Watercolor: OpenFreeMap's parks and water painted into a render target and cut into washes by blurred, noise-wandered thresholds, the land everything else, each stopping short of the streets by a wandering gap of bare paper, the great streets reserved as bold strokes of paper, the wider the bolder, widening as the map tilts so the far ones stay whole; the land swinging over kilometres between warm sienna and cool ochre, a rose wash over the dense core, patches of paper left unpainted; parks in two greens bleeding wet into their neighbours; the water deep teal at its banks under a dark pooled line, with tide lines inside it; a hard, dark, broken rim where each land wash dried, heaviest at its corners; buildings as crisp translucent glazes set a little off register with a dried edge on one side; backruns, pale with a darker edge, in the big washes; pigment settled in the paper's tooth, heavy in the water, lighter on the land, none in the parks; a warm rim to the sheet, and in tilted views the far side dissolving into the paper; names in warm sepia and deep blue.
